title: Wanted man killed by police the second such shooting in nine days
article: A man wanted for assault and unlawful confinement of a woman at a Gold Bar apartment was shot and killed by Edmonton police Wednesday night, the second deadly officer-involved shooting in just over a week.

Police were responding to the home near 47 Street and 101A Avenue just after 9 p.m. when the 26-year-old man left the residence and confronted officers before they opened fire. Officers administered first aid until EMS arrived but the man died at the scene.
The apartment in east Edmonton is the same location where a 28-year-old woman was reportedly assaulted over the course of several days, police said.
Earlier that day, around 2:30 p.m., officers were called to the home and found an injured woman who had been assaulted.
Police immediately ordered the arrest of the man on charges of two counts of assault causing bodily harm, intimidation, uttering threats as well as unlawful confinement.
Officers left the area but were called back to the home on Wednesday night after the man had reportedly returned.
The woman and the man were known to each other, police said in a statement early Thursday morning.

Alice Pobihushchyi lives in the Rivervalley Townhouse complex with her husband and five-year-old son. She said they didn't hear any gunshots Wednesday night but heard commotion outside and multiple dogs barking.
She said they looked out and saw police surrounding a man lying in the snow a few doors down.
"My husband heard him groaning and a few minutes after that we didn't hear him make noise," she said, adding an ambulance soon arrived.
Pobihushchyi and other residents in the area said they believe the couple were new tenants and kept to themselves.
"It was pretty scary knowing that there's families that live around here," said Pobihushchyi.
"Now we are concerned and we're probably not going to be staying here for too long, especially for the safety of our son."
Another resident said the townhomes are generally very quiet, which is why many young families choose to live there.
On Thursday morning, police tape remained hanging from a light fixture at the rear of the apartment and bloodied snow marked the western side of the complex.
No police officers were injured in the incident.
Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT), the province's police watchdog, has taken over the investigation into the shooting.

The death follows a Boxing Day police shooting when officers killed a man near 71 Street and 79 Avenue in the King Edward Park neighbourhood after he allegedly shot a gun at police during a "highrisk arrest."
Buck Evans was wanted on outstanding warrants and was considered "armed and dangerous" at the time of his arrest, ASIRT said.
ASIRT investigators said the 34-year-old shot at police after defying officers'orders and refusing to leave a red Chevrolet truck. Multiple officers also fired weapons.
Evans was taken to hospital shortly after the shootout but later died.

According to court records, Evans' previous convictions and charges go back to 2003. Most recently, warrants for Evans' arrest were issued Nov. 28 for possession of a controlled substance and failing to comply with his probation order.

In separate sentencings in February 2018 and January 2017, Evans received a lifetime ban on possessing firearms. He previously had a five-year firearms ban issued in 2005 and a 10-year ban issued in 2011.
Last year ASIRT was directed to investigate 21 police-involved shootings across the province, 11 of which were fatal.
Two of the 18 cases involved Edmonton Police Service officers while nine involved Calgary Police Service members.
The RCMP were involved in the remaining cases.
